stem: A new surveillance rule is tested in a group confirmed to be free of the target disease. Investigators want to know how well the rule avoids incorrectly classifying these people as cases. Which of the following quantities measures that ability?

options.label: A
options.text: Negative classifications divided by all disease-free people
options.explanation: Specificity measures correct negative classification among people who do not have the disease. The disease-free group is the denominator, and correctly negative results are the numerator.
options.misconception: No misconception: specificity counts correctly negative results among noncases.

options.label: B
options.text: Positive classifications divided by all disease-free people
options.explanation: This measures the false-positive fraction among people without disease. It complements specificity but counts errors, rather than the successful exclusions requested by the investigators.
options.misconception: Counts false-positive errors instead of successful disease exclusion.

options.label: C
options.text: True positive classifications divided by all positive results
options.explanation: This is positive predictive value, which starts with positive results. The specified study instead asks about correct classification within a group already known to be disease-free.
options.misconception: Confuses disease among positive results with negative classification of noncases.

options.label: D
options.text: True positive classifications divided by all people with disease
options.explanation: This is sensitivity, the detection fraction among people with disease. The investigators are assessing exclusion among people without disease, so a different denominator is required.
options.misconception: Substitutes detection among diseased people for exclusion among disease-free people.

options.label: E
options.text: True negative classifications divided by all negative results
options.explanation: This measures the fraction of negative results that are truly disease-free. Specificity instead includes all disease-free people, including those incorrectly classified as positive, in its denominator.
options.misconception: Uses negative results as the denominator instead of all disease-free people.

context:
Learning objective: Distinguish specificity from false-positive frequency and predictive value when evaluating a screening rule.

Specificity measures correct negative classification among people who do not have the disease. The disease-free group is the denominator, and correctly negative results are the numerator.
